draftNote: drafted · guessed · from the request of 2026-10-27 ('turn the current sandboxing ability of this system into a bolt on that can go into a new folder called Cells', then Sandboxie and Linux / WSL Linux cells) and the answers given that day: app/Cells as its own crate, backend and UI both moved, Sandboxie driven as an installed copy. Every answer below marked 'drafted' is the AI's reading, not a decision. solutionType is 'application' only because the form offers no 'library' type — Cells is a library that an application bolts in. Delete this field and the markers to accept.

purpose.question: What is the purpose of this solution?
purpose.answer: drafted · guessed — Where a command an app runs on somebody's behalf actually runs, as a bolt-on rather than as part of one app. Each place a command can run is a 'cell': this machine, an app-owned WSL distribution, a container per run today; Sandboxie (Windows) and a native Linux cell to come. A cell decides what to run and where, detects what this machine can really enforce, sets its boundary up on a press, and reports the truth about it — never a protection that detection did not prove. Swarm is its first host.

hosting.question: Where will it be hosted, deployed, or distributed?
hosting.answer: drafted · guessed — Not distributed on its own. Compiled into its host (Swarm) as a path dependency, and its panels bundled into the host's frontend. Windows and Linux, as the host is.

language.question: What language will it use?
language.answer: Rust for the cells; TypeScript + React for the panels that report them.

frameworks.question: What frameworks, libraries, or UI toolkit should it use?
frameworks.answer: drafted · guessed — No framework of its own. Rust: tokio for spawning and timeouts, serde, reqwest for fetching a policy, sha2 for its digest — the same versions as the host, so one build holds one copy. UI: React 19 components that take what they need from the host through small interfaces (CellsBackend), so the panels never assume Tauri or any transport.

authType.question: How does this solution authenticate or authorise callers/users?
authType.answer: None — it is a library inside a single-user local app with no login. A cell is a containment boundary for an agent, not an access-control boundary for people, and must never be described as one.

rolesOrClaims.question: Does it authorise by Claims or Roles?
rolesOrClaims.answer: Neither. Whatever roles the host has decide what is visible there; Cells knows nothing of them.

lookAndFeel.question: What is the overall look and feel?
lookAndFeel.answer: The panels Swarm already had, unchanged: a capability table of protections × cells, every verdict in words rather than a padlock or a tick, each with its reason.

stylingOrToolkit.question: What styling approach, component library, or UI toolkit?
stylingOrToolkit.answer: Plain CSS in ui/cells.css, using the host's theme variables rather than defining any. The host imports it after its own stylesheet.

interactionModel.question: How do people interact with it?
interactionModel.answer: Through the host's panels: choose where agents run, set a cell's boundary up on a press, read what each cell enforces on this machine.

configLocation.question: Where does it read/write its own config and data on disk?
configLocation.answer: It stores nothing of its own. The host stores which cell is chosen and passes it in; detection is re-read every time and never cached. What a cell sets up lives where that cell lives — the WSL distribution, the container image, the Sandboxie box.

errorLogging.question: How do we log errors and issues?
errorLogging.answer: It returns errors to its host as plain sentences and logs nothing itself; the host decides where they go.

documentation.question: How is this solution documented for its users or callers?

boilerplate.question: Start from a named boilerplate?
boilerplate.answer: None — extracted from Swarm's tooling/sandbox*.rs and three Admin panels in Round A.

fileLayout.question: What is the folder and file layout of this solution's repo?
answer: app/Cells/src/sandbox.rs — the seam: `wrap` and the capability `report`
app/Cells/src/sandbox_{detect,provision,run,docker,policy,intune}.rs — detection, set-up, the WSL and Docker backends, per-Solution deny policy, the device-policy export
app/Cells/src/seam.rs — finds every file that starts a process, for a host to prove its callers go through `wrap`
app/Cells/src/which.rs — PATH lookup, shared with the host
app/Cells/ui/ — the panels (SandboxTable, PolicySource, DevicePolicyExport), their types and cells.css
app/Cells/ui/__tests__/ — Vitest tests, run by the host's npm test

testing.question: What test framework should be used, and what kinds of tests?
testing.answer: TDD per the Project Brief's dev-rules. Rust: `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` from app/Cells — the host's cargo test does not run a dependency's tests. Live tests that need a real engine or distribution stay #[ignore]. UI: run by the host's `npm test` through the @cells alias.

baseline.question: Start from a named security baseline?

rules.question: Any extra security rules for this solution?
entries: No protection is ever reported as in force that detection did not prove on this machine — the rule the sandbox page was built on, and the one every new cell inherits.
A cell whose boundary cannot be honoured refuses to run the command; it never falls back to running it on this machine.
Anything that changes the machine (creating a distribution, building an image, configuring a box) happens on a press, prints everything it did, and stops at the first failure.
Every process a host starts on somebody's behalf goes through `sandbox::wrap`, held by a source-reading test in the host.
drafted · guessed — Third-party sandboxes are driven, never vendored or installed by this solution: Sandboxie-Plus is GPLv3 with a kernel driver, and this repository is MIT.

resources.question: What infrastructure resources does this solution need?

provisioning.question: How is infrastructure created, and by whom?
provisioning.answer: N/A — no server-side infrastructure. Built and tested by the host's pipeline (ci.yml and release.yml run Cells' cargo gates beside Swarm's).

environments.question: What environments exist, and which may the AI deploy to?
environments.answer: N/A — released only as part of its host.

mustNotDo.question: Anything this solution must NOT do / cannot deploy?

limits.question: Any limits (rate limits, payload size, memory, startup time, supported platforms)?
limits.answer: Windows and Linux, as the host. Each cell states which platforms it exists on; a cell that cannot exist on this platform is absent, not failed.

openQuestions: Should Cells be usable by an app other than Swarm? Round A keeps Swarm's own names inside it (the 'swarm' distribution, the agent image, `.swarm/policy.json`); making them a host's choice is a separate round.
Round B (a `Cell` trait) and Round C (Sandboxie): how does a Sandboxie run's work leave the box — the run folder opened through to the real disk, or its changes recovered afterwards?
Round D (native Linux): is bubblewrap the cell, and is building it before the MVP the right order? The project's goals put agent governance second.
Should Round 12 of the Agent Sandbox brief (an honest panel on Linux, Docker finished) be built before the Linux cell? It is planned and not built.
